repairsTips.text: Sometimes it's better to carry all the parts with you during a repair so no one steals them. The alternative is to hide the parts in a container that is unlikely to be checked, or in a container closer to the repair site (for convenience), but at the very bottom of the container. From time to time, glance at the electrical panel, the supercomputer and the air purifier. This way you'll make sure the parts are in place and nothing has been stolen, and at the same time check whether someone has already brought the needed parts — this saves time searching for and crafting repair items.
Just in case, you can keep on you the staff badge, the classified facility blueprints and the staff-room keycard — they may be needed in the next repair stages.
When overloaded, drop the heavy parts on the floor, gather items from containers up to the yellow bar, and drag the dropped parts to the workbench by holding LMB and moving the mouse.
Pin the repair recipe so the parts you need stay in front of you. It works just like pinning crafting recipes, so you no longer have to remember what is missing every time.

mascot.tagline: Details solve cases. Better to write down too much than to miss what matters.

items.text: Collecting fingerprints from unlocked doors is allowed. But it's better to ask players directly first — if they refuse, lift prints from the places they touched. That way you both interact with the cast and, if you're caught, easily parry with the fact that you had already tried to obtain the prints earlier.

Lockpicks can be used to break into a dormitory room door — you don't need to ask permission for this, even at the very start of the game. However, breaking a door open with a crowbar specifically (not picking it with a lockpick) at the very start of the game without an RP reason is considered a violation of rule 4.3.
Get hold of: food, zip ties, a bandage, batteries for the UV flashlight. Don't be afraid to ask other players for help
Recharge the UV flashlight at the electrical panel or with batteries. It lasts for 20 uses at 5% per collected fingerprint. If you just shine the flashlight, no charge is spent.
Copy the notepad's contents to the clipboard ([[CTRL+C]]) — if a culprit edits the text or steals the notepad, you'll be able to restore it ([[CTRL+V]])
Keep two notepads. The second — in a safe in case of death or theft. Inform trusted players.
Double-check the recorded fingerprints. You can make a mistake in your notes and then build theories on that mistake, only to discover it at the trial itself.
Record the time of Monokuma events. For the masquerade and the blackout, note the start and the end.
Close doors — the killer will have to leave a fingerprint to open them, and waste time.
Via «Inspect» (the [[T]] button on hover), check players for gloves and night-vision devices, and note them in the notepad
Get to know the cast better by talking with players. Watch who sticks with whom and where they go — this helps you understand the dynamics and potentially uncover motives even before a murder

Check fingerprints at the workbench in the gym and the medical workbench in the medical office. Keep in mind: a workbench and a medical workbench are also on the 2nd floor of the abandoned dormitory and in the chemistry laboratory (4F).
Record players' bloody hands — even if they claim there's no connection to the murder.

Players set traps all over the map — especially often inside other players' rooms. A stunned, sedated, or worse, dead detective is no help to anyone. So be careful and watch your step. By the way, the teleport points are fixed — 17 on the first floor + 2 in the boiler room + 1 in the garden by the dormitory, 9 on the second floor, 8 on the third floor, 7 on the fourth floor, and 8 on the fifth floor. Killers can set traps near them in advance, so be careful.
Collect gunpowder in the boiler room and the medical office to rule out the making of explosives or a trap. Store it in a safe with yourself or with trusted players.
Patrol the school constantly. The mere presence of a detective can prevent a murder or provide important testimony

Sometimes you can try to bait players into leaving prints: ask a player to «check» an item or a location under some pretext, ask for some object, or just watch a player and note what they touch. But there's a small risk that someone else's prints were already there, so always double-check or use elimination against what you already know.

Zip ties and handcuffs let you restrict a player's actions: they can move, but can't open doors or interact with anything. A bag over the head blocks their view but doesn't stop them from discovering a body. And tape stuck over the mouth prevents speaking in voice chat.

You can also tether a player while they're in zip ties or handcuffs. Grab them in a hold and pick the point you want to tie them to. That way they can't run off. And by the way, a teleport event will still move a tethered player — but they'll stay in the zip ties or handcuffs at the new spot.

Zip ties are cut with a kitchen knife, a katana, or a cleaver. Handcuffs are opened only with a screwdriver (though you can do it without one if you put them on the player yourself). You can also put them on yourself, but you won't be able to free yourself.
Keep in mind that relationships between players are very important, since conflicts and personal animosity can become a motive for murder.
Corners are easier to check in third-person thanks to the wider view. But it's better to lift fingerprints in first-person.
At first, hit «check the watch» after every encounter with another player; once the habit sets in and you get a better sense of when it's worth checking and when not, you'll use it only as needed.

Check the fingerprints on the knife stand in the kitchen: it's the only place in the whole academy where the kitchen knife and the cleaver spawn. This helps narrow the suspect list when the murder weapon is one of those two.

Okay, this tip sounds like paranoia, but I still have to write it down: try not to stand still during a conversation — a zip tie goes on in seconds. Move a little from side to side. If you do have to stand, press your back to a wall and control the widest possible field of view. When lifting fingerprints, ask the player to step back a bit. Looks weird? It does. But you're unlikely to get zip-tied.

You can use voice-typing software (Wispr Flow, for example) to dictate notes straight into the detective's notepad — it's faster than typing by hand. The program, for the record, only transcribes speech into text.

If you're locked in the freezer and not cuffed or zip-tied, you can lay out meat from containers or items from your inventory in the shape of the killer's initials — or, if you have it, just write the killer's name in the notepad.

A trap can be disarmed with any object — even a coin, but rectangular props are the handiest: easier to toss and hit the tripwire. With an explosive trap, be careful and keep your distance so the blast wave doesn't catch you. A screwdriver also lets you actually PICK UP a trap.

There are four keycards in the game: the staff room, the utility rooms, the abandoned dormitory floor — and the Academy Head's keycard, which combines all three. Every keycard grants access to its namesake location, but the utility-rooms keycard is worth highlighting: it opens the utility room on the 3rd floor and the one between floors 3 and 4. There's also a utility room on the 5th floor, but access there is open even without a keycard. The garden by the dormitory and floors 4 and 5 are reachable only through trials or repairs — keycards don't work there.

To lift a fingerprint from surfaces — doors, lockers, the workbench, the medical lab — take the UV flashlight in hand, aim at the print, and press F: the print goes straight into your inventory. How to lift prints from an item: RMB on the item → «Inspect» → hover over the hints until the progress bar fills — properties open up: «Bloodied», «Fingerprints» with a player's letter — or «Cleanup traces» if someone wiped it. To take a print as evidence, press RMB → «Lift fingerprints» → pick the one you need in the submenu. Works with any item.

detail.toggleLabel: Show video: how to lift fingerprints

items.text: Shoeprints are lifted the same way as fingerprints — when prompted, choose the «shoeprints» profile. There are 16 unique fingerprints and 16 unique shoeprints in the game. Sometimes you can do without a UV scan: say, if a bloody footprint was found next to the body, you can ask several players to step into the blood puddle near the body and compare the prints visually. Then, by elimination, identify the potential killer without collecting a single print.

Early-trial strategy: at the start of the game, drop by the tool rack in the shop — the adjustable wrench, hammer, and crowbar spawn there. Write down or memorize what spawned. Then combine that with a hammer check: everyone's own hammer spawns in their cabinet, and if at the trial someone can't produce a hammer and clearly explain where it went — that's already a great lead. In early trials with little evidence, this method can really catch the culprit red-handed. Also keep in mind that bludgeoning weapons spawn in other places too (see below): the hammer also randomly spawns in two toolboxes in the gym (10% each) and on the rack in the shop (35%). Also in the gym — the lead pipe (10%); by the workbench — the baseball bat (20%), which also spawns on the 2nd floor in the giraffe room (20%). The crowbar, besides the rack, can appear in the red locker in the incinerator (15%).

phases.title: During the investigation
phases.subtitle: A body has been found — every minute counts

mascot.name: Чиаки Нанами
mascot.tagline: Every murder is a level. Find the pattern, and you'll solve it.

items.text: Press G to highlight evidence at the crime scene. Hold the button while you walk around the room — that way you'll spot evidence even behind objects.

Ask players not to touch the body, since the killer may have left fingerprints on the victim. Extra touches make finding the killer's prints harder. It rarely works, since everyone usually starts searching the poor soul, but it's still worth a try.

There are two kinds of gloves in the game. Plain «gloves» are reusable: while worn, every print you leave is smeared. Disposable gloves also smear prints, but last for 10 uses, after which they tear and from then on leave ordinary prints. Prints, in turn, come in four kinds: ordinary, smeared, bloody, and bloody-smeared. Ordinary and bloody prints let you identify the owner. But ordinary-smeared or bloody-smeared ones, unfortunately, can't be traced to a person. Ordinary and smeared prints (not bloody) can't be seen without a UV flashlight.

Breaking in with a crowbar leaves no fingerprints on the door — the killer can use this to hide their presence at that location. But there's a side effect: a loud noise that alerts everyone nearby to the break-in.
The «blood puddle» clue confirms that the body wasn't moved and the victim died right there.

Traces of traps and throwing weapons help reconstruct the picture: what exactly was used and how much. Downside: they can be wiped away with a mop before you arrive. But luckily, a death description from a trap or a weapon in the Monokuma File can't be wiped away even with a mop.

A killer, or some trickster, or sometimes just a troll can wipe evidence with a mop: footprints and the blood puddle, fingerprints and shoeprints, traces of traps and throwing weapons. If you arrive at a murder scene and see none of the above, it doesn't mean it was never there. It may mean someone simply did a thorough job.

Check containers' weight and scroll to the bottom cells, or use auto-sort — evidence is often hidden at the bottom. But evidence can also lie around simply as props in stashes — that is, outside a container, behind some object.

There are three kinds of shoeprints in the game: bloody (if you stepped in the victim's blood puddle), wet (if you went into the water in the bathhouse or the pool), and dirty (if you were in the garden by the cafeteria or the garden by the dormitory). The effect lasts for 10 steps and then fades, and those 10 steps in turn disappear after 12 in-game hours or 10 real minutes. They're best seen through a UV flashlight.

There's always a chance that by the start of the investigation the killer is already dead. For example, the trap could have been set in a previous chapter by the victim or the killer. Another situation: the killer could have committed the murder and then been killed by another player.

After striking a blow, the text «bloody hands» appears over the player's head. However, if the blow was struck while wearing gloves, there's no such label — the gloves become bloody, but the hands stay clean. It's also worth noting that bloody gloves can't be washed off in a sink; the most you can do is wipe them with a rag.

The bloody-hands effect appears only when you strike a player with a cold weapon BEFORE the investigation (you can't get this effect during the investigation) — not from dragging, not from a punch, and not from picking up a bloodied weapon. Three cases:
subItems: Without gloves and without a disguise — ordinary bloody prints.
In a disguise without gloves — a smeared bloody print, but the bloody-hands effect remains (take off the disguise and they become ordinary bloody prints).

With gloves (and in a disguise with gloves) — only the gloves become bloody, the hands are clean. The exception is torn disposable gloves: in them the hands become bloody after a blow, and all smeared prints become bloody. However, once those gloves tear, the prints become ordinary, not bloody, even if you open doors or containers in them.

items.text: The «ordinary hit» (LMB), the «swing hit» (when you hold and release LMB), and the right-mouse-button hit are described identically in the Monokuma File. Exception: the katana on a right-mouse-button attack is described differently.

If a player dies of hunger or lack of sleep while in zip ties or handcuffs (the Monokuma File should retain marks of the restraints), the guilty one is whoever put them on. And yes, this murder method is a gray area, since by the rules we can't hold another player against their will for more than 5 minutes, but no one says you won't have to deal with cases like this. So forewarned is forearmed.
In the case of death from hypothermia in the freezer or overheating in the bathhouse, the guilty one is whoever closed the door.

Death from hypothermia occurs after roughly 3 minutes 31 seconds of real time. Overheating kills faster, in roughly 2 minutes 28 seconds of real time. Keeping this in mind, we can look at the victim's time of death and guess when they ended up there.

It's useful to keep in mind that the killer gets a notification when a victim triggers their trap. They also have the killer's instinct, which for 20 seconds after a murder shows the positions of other players within a medium radius as a red cloud. This lets them plan an escape route and fabricate an alibi.

A killer can restrain themselves — putting on zip ties, handcuffs, tape, a bag — to earn an alibi with the words «I was tied up and couldn't have killed». But the only thing they can take off on their own is the bag.
If one of a food's components is poisoned, the food becomes poisoned too. Example: poisoned cheese that is later used to make a sandwich.

A single killer, or a killer-and-accomplice pair, can't commit more than two murders per chapter. If there are three or more bodies, then most likely there are at least two independent killers on the server. For this violation there's an automatic mass-kill penalty: when the killer kills a third player, they drop dead themselves and their victims come back to life.

Killing a player when there's more than one witness is forbidden. Exception: there are four people in the room — the first is the killer, the second the accomplice, and the killer and accomplice are about to kill the third and fourth. Practical takeaway: you're safe in a group of at least three people, and better — four or more. If the rule is broken, don't hesitate to file a report and attach a recording from the game.

A fake alibi doesn't always mean deliberate lying. Players confuse the time, forget where they were, write it down wrong, or misread the in-game clock. First clarify — maybe the person just made a mistake. But it also means you can't always trust players' alibis. At the very least, it's better to have as many people as possible confirm it.
Blows to the body after the victim's death leave no wounds — the Monokuma File records only injuries sustained while alive.

Damage descriptions in the Monokuma File go in chronological order. But secondary condition details (like being put to sleep) are always appended after the injuries — regardless of when they happened. So if a player was put to sleep with a somnus grenade, woke up, and was then killed — the Monokuma File will show the murder weapon first, and the sleep effect after.
The investigation time depends on the opened gates — 7 minutes at the start of the game, +2 minutes for each opened floor, up to a maximum of 15 minutes.
During the investigation you can't take damage or die. Stamina, alertness, and satiety aren't spent. You also can't repair the electrical panel, the supercomputer, or the air purifier.
While a player is unconscious, they're immune to fall damage, Molotov cocktails, poisons and being crushed. But unfortunately, that still won't save them from explosives or melee weapons.
Fists deal 8–12 damage per hit (the same for all characters), but deal no damage to a player at 20 health or below — and yes, you can't kill with fists.

Record the time of each repair stage: that way you'll know exactly when the boiler room, the garden by the dormitory, and the upper floors opened. It helps catch false alibis (for example, when someone says «I was by the boiler room», but it hadn't even opened yet at that time) and lets you reconstruct routes: who could even physically have been in the right place at the right time.

Establish the alibi time window for this murder. Recall whom you yourself can give an alibi to for that time. How to do it? Take the time of the murder and listen to other players' alibis for that time and around it. Having determined the murder location, hear out the players' testimony and gauge whether any of them could physically have been at the murder scene or not. And most importantly — can anyone confirm their alibi? (one person isn't always enough, since they may turn out to be an accomplice)
Check with other players who last saw the victim: when, where, and whether anyone was nearby.

Infer the killer's route: where they came from, where they could have washed their hands or the weapon. Sinks are in the restrooms by the gym and the dormitory, on the abandoned floor, on the 2nd and 4th floors, in the medical office, the laundry, the kitchen, the dormitory rooms, the art-room back room, and the chemistry laboratory.

If you have time left, check your own room for traps at the end of the investigation. Sometimes a wrongdoer can use the investigation time to set a trap that someone is meant to trigger at the start of the next chapter.

The 3rd-floor utility room is a junction of several routes: the gym bridge, the 3rd floor, the vent into the library's archive room, the 2nd-floor men's restroom, the pool, and the boiler room. It lets you move quickly between floors 1, 2, and 3. Keep this in mind when reconstructing the killer's route.
A car wheel and a fuel canister work as a step-up and help you reach evidence located above the character model.

A wheel behind a container — from it you can see the gloves dropped on top.

items.text: If several people poison the same food, who do you think is the killer? The correct answer: priority goes first to the poison's strength; and if the poison is the same, the killer is whoever poisoned it first.

Monokuma takes away a suicide's body after 5 real minutes along with all its inventory. This makes the body an ideal place to get rid of evidence. The detective, in turn, can dump weapons, traps, and gunpowder there — and check it for evidence too.
Various combo-kill cases that we managed to test at players' request:
subItems: Case 1: if a person dropped a cabbage (it's the model of the «vegetables» item) and another struck it with a katana and hit the victim, the killer is the one who threw the cabbage. The Monokuma File will show «blunt-object injuries»; the katana that struck the projectile isn't mentioned, nor is the kinetic projectile that's usually noted for a cabbage kill. And yes, you shouldn't do this.

subItems.text: Case 2: if a player was tied up, knocked out, or grabbed in a hold and thrown into someone else's Molotov, the killer is whoever threw the Molotov.
subItems: Player A threw the Molotov, Player B zip-tied and tethered the victim. (Killer: Player A)
Player A tied the victim up and threw the Molotov, Player B grabbed them in a hold and threw them into the fire (Killer: Player A)
Player A tied the victim up and threw the Molotov, Player B grabbed them in a hold and did not let go until the victim died (Killer: Player B)
Case 3: if one person tied someone up and another pushed them in the gym, the killer is the one who pushed.
Case 4: in a prop kill using a door, the killer is the one who placed the object (not the one who opened or closed the door). This is a bug abuse, so we don't do it.

Case 5: if two players were locked in the freezer and one put zip ties on the other, the killer is considered to be the one who applied the zip ties (and the killer of the second player is, of course, whoever closed the door).

phases.title: During the trial
phases.subtitle: Steer the conversation, stick to the facts

items.text: Note: at the start of the trial, Monokuma tells us exactly whose case we're investigating. This matters, since sometimes there are several bodies and before the trial begins it's unclear — one killer or not.

At the start of the trial, immediately announce the murder location, the murder weapon, the time of death, and so on, so everyone is on the same page. Not everyone conducts an investigation, and not everyone understands what's even going on. Also don't forget to state your route (that is, your movement between locations and the exact timings) and your alibi.

Please don't wait for someone to say something useful on their own. In the chaos it'll never happen — plus you can simply miss important information when everyone's talking at once. So run the case and bring structure yourself. Ask everyone one at a time. And you don't really have to crack the case single-handedly. Your role is to provide all the information you managed to gather and organize the conversation so that, as a group, you can solve the case. That's what a detective's job is.

If the trial descends into chaos and you can't properly talk to a specific player or just voice critical information — call a cross-debate. Everyone goes quiet and the two of you get two minutes one-on-one.

Even if you didn't manage to find evidence during the investigation, remember: you're not starting from zero. You have alibis, some of which you probably already gathered during the investigation. Some you can give yourself — you were somewhere too and saw something. The rest of the alibis you close at the trial. And you can start not in order, but with those you suspect most.

When there's very little information, watch behavior rather than words. Someone dodges the topic. Someone stays silent when they should answer. Someone tries to seize control of the conversation. These are little clues too.
Remember that you can't immediately trust an alibi if only two players confirm it — they could easily turn out to be accomplices.
Don't fixate too much on one theory: lock in the current one, and then, if there's time, try to build an alternative, compare — and only then choose.

Honestly, a trial without evidence is, unfortunately, the default. And if you've found even one clue, you're already at an advantage. Learn to work through trials purely on testimony and analysis. Once you learn to work with a shortage of information, you'll crack cases with evidence many times faster. If you don't have the information to build a theory — ask for more. Widen the questioning time range: «who was doing what an hour before this», «who saw the victim earlier». If people stay quiet — ask them to say everything they remember, any little detail.

phases.subtitle: Debrief and work on your mistakes

mascot.name: K1-B0
mascot.tagline: Every game is data. Analyze, update, play again.

items.text: Talk with players (especially the killers) in the lobby — clarify details and go over mistakes

characters.name: Макото Наэги
characters.description: An ordinary high-schooler who got into the academy through a lottery. His main strength is unshakable optimism and faith in his friends.

characters.name: Бьякуя Тогами
characters.description: Heir to the powerful Togami financial empire, who came through a brutal family struggle for the right to lead. He treats taking part in the killing game as an intellectual contest, regarding everyone else as mere pawns.

characters.name: Киётака Ишимару
characters.description: Grandson of a former prime minister, who has devoted his life to restoring his family's honor through fanatical adherence to the rules. Kiyotaka despises laziness and believes that hard work matters more than talent. He is always in motion, maintaining perfect discipline, but his bluntness keeps him from noticing hidden nuances.

characters.name: Кёко Киригири
characters.description: A mysterious girl whose past is shrouded in secrecy even to herself. She possesses phenomenal observation and deduction skills inherited from a family of hereditary detectives. Kyoko is used to suppressing her emotions, which gives her a colossal advantage in survival.

characters.name: Саяка Майзоно
characters.description: The Ultimate Pop Sensation and leader of a popular idol group. Behind her dazzling stage smile hides incredible determination and a willingness to do anything to preserve her dream.

characters.name: Селестия Люденберг
characters.description: The queen of gothic lies, weaving a web of illusions. She rejected her own name for the sake of an invented aristocratic ideal. Her poker face is flawless, and other people's lives are to her merely chips on the roulette baize.

characters.name: Джунко Эношима
characters.description: A perfect soldier hiding her crosshair behind a camera lens. Beneath the mask of a capricious fashion model hide the flawless reflexes of a mercenary who knows neither mercy nor the fear of death.

characters.name: Токо Фукава
characters.description: A tormented muse whose words are sharper than scissors. An outcast locked in a cage of paranoia and complexes. Her brilliant novels are born of pain, and in the depths of her broken mind sleeps something far darker and more uncontrollable.

characters.name: Аой Асахина
characters.description: A bubbling stream of sincere emotion. A dazzlingly cheerful swimmer whose energy overflows. She cannot hide her feelings and is ready to throw herself into the storm to protect those she calls friends.

characters.name: Сакура Огами
characters.description: An indestructible rock with the soul of a noble samurai. The strongest person on the planet, whose terrifying might serves only as a shield for the innocent. A warrior who has devoted her life to training and attaining true serenity.

characters.name: Хифуми Ямада
characters.description: A creator of 2D illusions, lost in reality. He rejected the cruel world of people for the comfort of manga and anime, becoming the absolute master of fictional worlds and plots.

characters.name: Леон Кувата
characters.description: A rebellious soul torn between a baseball bat and an electric guitar. A hot-tempered and impulsive rebel who is used to achieving success effortlessly, without thinking about the consequences of his actions.

characters.name: Ясухиро Хагакурэ
characters.description: A carefree wanderer along the lines of probability. Cowardly, lazy and absurdly naive. His predictions come true only a third of the time, but his ability to drift along the current of absurdity makes him surprisingly resilient.

characters.name: Мукуро Икусаба
characters.description: A nameless blade that does not know its own desires. An elite mercenary of 'Fenrir' whose life is devoted to carrying out orders. A living weapon devoid of empathy, yet blindly devoted to the one person dear to her.

characters.name: Джунко Эношима
characters.description: The deadly conductor of the orchestra of Ultimate Despair. A genius for whom the predictability of the world has become an unbearable torment. She craves to destroy everything in order to savor the genuine, unfeigned pain of humanity.

characters.name: Чихиро Фуджисаки
characters.description: A brilliant programmer who created advanced AI. A fragile and shy youth who desperately longs to become stronger in order to overcome his inner fears.

characters.name: Мондо Овада
characters.description: The second leader of Japan's largest biker gang, the 'Crazy Diamonds'. Mondo hides his vulnerability behind a mask of brute force and a short temper. Years of street fights have made him incredibly enduring and able to carry heavy loads, but his diet and lifestyle are far from ideal.

characters.name: Хаджимэ Хината
characters.description: A blank canvas among bright colors. A man whose ordinariness became his curse and his main weapon. Rejected by the talent system, he stubbornly seeks the truth, refusing to bend under the weight of others' genius.

characters.name: Нагито Комаэда
characters.description: A fanatic of the idea of Ultimate Hope. He balances on the thin line between genius and madness. Because of a cycle of incredible luck and cruel tragedies, his mind is broken, and his self-sacrifice knows no bounds.

characters.name: Гандам Танака
characters.description: A lonely lord of illusions. Behind a veil of theatrical mysticism and tales of demons hides a sensitive soul, able to find common ground with any beast, yet endlessly far from understanding people.

characters.name: Фуюхико Кузурю
characters.description: Heir to a criminal throne, locked in a teenager's body. Behind his ferocious gaze and rudeness lies a desperate desire to prove his strength without relying on the status and influence of his deadly family.

characters.name: Ибуки Миода
characters.description: A chord shattering the silence. A girl living at maximum volume. She turns every second into a bright performance, charging those around her with her primal, uncontrollable rock energy.

characters.name: Соня Невермайнд
characters.description: Royal grace. A flawless princess who studied the art of war and leadership. Behind her radiant smile hides a frightening but sincere interest in serial killers and Japanese occultism.

characters.name: Чиаки Нанами
characters.description: A sleeping strategist of digital worlds. The Ultimate Gamer, able to calculate any algorithm and find a way out of a dead end. In reality she is slow and drowsy, but her logic never falters once the game begins in earnest.

characters.name: Микан Цумики
characters.description: A broken angel of mercy. A girl whose body and soul are covered in scars from others' cruelty. She begs for attention, humbling herself before everyone, but in the operating room her talent as a surgeon borders on divine intervention.

characters.name: Пеко Пекояма
characters.description: A living blade of the Kuzuryu clan. A girl who voluntarily destroyed the person within herself to become a flawless weapon for her master. Her loyalty is absolute, and her strikes are lightning-fast.

characters.name: Махиру Коидзуми
characters.description: An uncompromising lens of justice. A photographer whose shots are meant to preserve smiles. She has a sharp character and does not tolerate irresponsibility, always placing the group's well-being above her own ambitions.

characters.name: Аканэ Овари
characters.description: An untamable animal instinct locked in a human body. A child of the slums, used to surviving by fists and speed. She does not dwell on the complicated, preferring to solve problems in a fight or at the dinner table.

characters.name: Хиёко Сайонджи
characters.description: A poisonous flower of traditional dance. Behind the appearance of an innocent angel hides a cruel mocker who loves to humiliate those weaker than her. Her venom is merely a shield behind which a frightened, fragile child hides.

characters.name: Бьякуя Тогами
characters.description: A shadow without a face or name. A perfect chameleon, able to wear someone else's life better than the original. Despite the deception, he possesses true nobility, ready to protect those who trusted his false identity.

characters.name: Нэкомару Нидай
characters.description: A roaring flame of team spirit. A coach whose boiling energy and frightening physical might can revive even the dead. He is ready to sacrifice himself just so his charges reach the summit.

characters.name: Тэрутэру Ханамура
characters.description: A virtuoso of flavor with sinful thoughts. A chef hiding his provincial origins behind the facade of a metropolitan gourmet. Incredibly lecherous, yet devoted with all his soul to his mother and the culinary art.

characters.name: Казуичи Сода
characters.description: A creator of mechanisms with forever trembling hands. A brilliant mechanic able to assemble an escape shuttle from a heap of scrap metal. A paranoid coward whose fears constantly get the better of his logic.

characters.name: Рёко Отонаши
characters.description: Lost in the labyrinths of her own mind. A girl whose memories slip through her fingers, leaving only emptiness. Her personality lives on the pages of a notebook, but behind the veil of amnesia hides a frighteningly sharp analytical mind.

characters.name: Шуичи Сайхара
characters.description: A detective hiding his gaze from the harsh truth under the brim of his cap. He possesses brilliant deduction but is desperately afraid of the suffering his revelations bring to people. He is forced to overcome his fear in order to survive.

characters.name: Кокичи Ома
characters.description: A liar dancing on bones. A maestro of chaos whose true motives are hidden behind a thousand crying and laughing masks. He turns any tragedy into a farce, always staying several steps ahead of his victims.

characters.name: K1-B0
characters.description: A steel body with a human heart. A robot possessing a complex AI that strives to understand the warmth of the human soul. He reacts painfully to prejudice and desperately tries to prove that he is more than just a machine.

characters.name: Кайто Момота
characters.description: A blazing meteor piercing the darkness of logic. An astronaut for whom emotions and faith in friends matter more than any proof. A foolish but incredibly charismatic leader, able to ignite hope in the most despairing hearts.

characters.name: Рантаро Амами
characters.description: A calm harbor in the eye of the storm. A youth who forgot his talent but did not lose his composure. An experienced survivor who smiles in the face of danger and secretly plays his own game against the system.

characters.name: Корекиё Шингуджи
characters.description: A refined connoisseur of human tragedy. An anthropologist whose knowledge of the world's cultures borders on a sickly obsession. Behind his bandages hides a perverse mind, fascinated by the beauty of death and suffering.

characters.name: Гонта Гокухара
characters.description: The innocent soul of a forest giant. A huge and frighteningly strong youth raised in the wild. He dreams of becoming a true gentleman, is always ready to help, but is utterly helpless against cunning and lies.

characters.name: Каэде Акамацу
characters.description: A melody of unity, sounding in spite of fear. A kind and resolute pianist able to unite a scattered crowd into a single orchestra. She is ready to sacrifice everything so her friends can hear the final chord of freedom.

characters.name: Маки Харукава
characters.description: A scarlet flower grown on a battlefield. A flawless assassin hiding her bloody trade behind the mask of an unsociable caregiver. She has built a wall of ice around herself, panic-stricken at the thought of growing attached to anyone.

characters.name: Тенко Чабашира
characters.description: An unstoppable whirlwind of Neo-Aikido. An emotional, loud and endlessly naive girl. She directs all her energy toward protecting other girls and fiercely fighting the threat of 'degenerate males' she has invented.

characters.name: Миу Ирума
characters.description: A golden mind shackled by her own complexes. A brilliant inventor whose arrogance and vulgarity are merely a loud defense. At the slightest pressure she shrinks, baring a timid and insecure nature.

characters.name: Химико Юмено
characters.description: A weary mage hiding her tears behind tricks. An illusionist who stubbornly passes off her tricks as real magic. Chronically lazy and apathetic, she hides from cruel reality in a shell of eternal drowsiness.

characters.name: Кируми Тоджо
characters.description: A perfect mechanism of self-sacrifice in a maid's lace. Her devotion to duty is absolute, and her skills are boundless. She regards her own life merely as a tool for serving society and her master.

characters.name: Цумуги Широганэ
characters.description: A faceless spectator trying on others' fates. A cosplayer who calls herself 'completely ordinary'. She dissolves into the crowd, preferring to watch the unfolding drama with a fanatical gleam in her eyes.

characters.name: Анджи Ёнага
characters.description: A serene conduit of another's will, brush in hand. An exotic priestess of the god Atua. Behind her sweet voice and naive smile hides a frightening ability to subjugate people, turning them into a fanatical flock.

characters.name: Рёма Хоши
characters.description: A faded star wandering in the gloom of his own past. A former tennis player whose hands are bloodied up to the elbow with the mafia. He voluntarily gave up his future, considering his life a waste of oxygen.

characters.name: Комару Наэги
characters.description: A girl who stepped beyond her own ordinariness. Finding herself at the epicenter of madness without any outstanding talents, she is forced to clench her fists to overcome her fear and find rays of hope.

characters.name: Джатаро Кемури
characters.description: A terrified creator of ugly beauty. A child in a mask who sincerely believes in his own repulsiveness. He finds his perverse comfort in creating frightening dioramas and meekly accepting others' hatred.

characters.name: Масару Даймон
characters.description: A broken champion shouting about his superiority. A boy whose showy bravery and hyperactivity hide deep scars from adult cruelty. The leader of the Warriors of Hope, desperately seeking recognition.

characters.name: Нагиса Шингецу
characters.description: A glass genius crushed under the weight of others' ambitions. A child with a scientist's intellect whose psyche was destroyed by parental experiments. He longs to create a paradise for children, sacrificing his own childhood to logic.

characters.name: Котоко Уцуги
characters.description: A porcelain doll baring her fangs. Behind an obsession with all things 'cute' and ringing laughter hides a tormented actress who turned her pain into sadistic cruelty toward all adults.

characters.name: Монака Това
characters.description: A laughing puppeteer in a wheelchair. A brilliant sociopath with an angelic face, skillfully pulling the strings of others' traumas. She revels in power, striving to become the true successor of Ultimate Despair.

events.name: Despair Roulette
events.description: When no murders have happened for a long stretch, the Academy's headmaster puts on a show of his own. One participant becomes the Shooter; everyone else can only hope for luck.
events.note: The event can trigger only once per game.

sections.title: Trigger conditions
items: 45 minutes have passed since the game started and nobody has been eliminated;
the breaker box has been repaired and nobody had been eliminated before that point;
60 minutes have passed since a new chapter began and nobody was eliminated during it;
if the players survived the first Class Trial but the breaker box was never repaired, the event fires once the Supercomputer is repaired.

sections.title: How the event plays out
items: Monokuma picks one player at random — the Shooter.
Six random pairs of players are presented to the Shooter in turn.
The game picks between 0 and 2 live rounds and distributes them randomly across the six shots.
In each round the Shooter picks one of three targets: themselves, the first player, or the second player.

sections.title: Worth knowing
items: The full sequence involves 13 participants: one Shooter and six pairs of players.
The number of live rounds varies from 0 to 2, and in each of the six rounds the Shooter picks one of three targets — the event has no fixed chance of death.
If the Shooter dies by shooting themselves, the remaining shots stop: doing so saves between 0 and 2 players, depending on where the live rounds sit.

images.caption: The six-shot sequence as the other participants see it

tips: Events repeat roughly every 12–14 in-game hours. The countdown starts from the beginning of an event, not from its end.
Even ordinary Monokuma messages (random broadcasts) count as an event.
Note the moment of every event in your notebook. For a blackout and a masquerade, always log the start and the end: it helps reconstruct alibis and understand when the killer could act unseen.
Understanding the timings lets you predict the next event and, for example, gather the cast in one place for an alibi.
Monokuma events do not work during the investigation.
broadcasts: “The tastiest despair comes from the betrayal of someone close.”
“Nobody's killing anybody? How boring. It's making me yawn.”
“Today is a great day for despair. Thooough, any day will do.”
“Do you feel it too? It's the smell of fear and poorly hidden intentions.”
“Monokuma's tip of the day: trust your friends — they're the easiest to kill(?).”
“You know I'm watching you. Even now. Especially now.”
“Careful, there's a killer next to you. Just kidding. Or am I?”
“Sometimes I think you forget who's in charge here. Just a reminder.”
“I've already got the 'Body Discovered' sign ready, and you're still dragging it out.”
“Puhuhuhu. So quiet, even suspicious. Have you decided to be good people?”
“Hug each other more often — it's more convenient... for a stab in the back.”

poisonNotes: A Somnus grenade, sleeping pills and an electroshock let you stun or put a poisoned player to sleep and pause the poison’s timer — that buys time to craft the cure. Once the player comes round, the timer resumes from where it stopped.

If you stun a player before the poison has taken effect (that is, before the «taken → onset» timer runs out), the poison’s timer keeps running while they are unconscious and can expire before they come round, neutralising the poison’s effect.
A player cannot be poisoned while they are unconscious.
